title: Align OpenAI function protocol with Redwood tool proxy + streaming fragment reassembly
author: Maya Chen
ci_checks: perf-smoke: pass (median generation latency +4% under added framing)
commits: init: experimental adapter and spec mapping for OpenAI-style function calls
impl: map OpenAI function schemas to Redwood tool schemas with type coercion rules
stream: implement streaming fragment reassembly for tool outputs and tool_choice events
tests: add unit + integration tests for tool proxy and streaming reassembly
docs: add migration notes and example for structured tool outputs
fix: edgecase when tool emits partial JSON across SSE chunks (buffering bug)
chore: update changelog and Linear links
description:
Motivation: Customers using the OpenAI-compatible API expect two behaviors we haven't fully matched: (1) function/tool call semantics (including explicit 'tool_choice' hints and the way tool outputs are framed back into assistant messages) and (2) stable streaming behavior for tool outputs that may be emitted across multiple SSE/body fragments. This PR implements a compatibility layer that translates OpenAI-style function call requests into Redwood tool proxy invocations and reassembles streaming fragments so that downstream clients (and SDKs) receive consistent assistant/message+tool events.

Summary of changes: implement a deterministic mapping from OpenAI function JSON schemas to Redwood tool parameter schemas (coercion, optional/nullable handling, and enum mappings); introduce a small protocol shim that emits explicit assistant messages for tool invocation lifecycle (invocation.started, invocation.output, invocation.finished) while preserving Redwood's internal tool routing; add a streaming_reassembler that buffers partial UTF-8/JSON fragments and emits well-formed events to the OpenAI-compat SSE stream; update docs with migration guidance and example prompts; add unit and integration tests.

Design notes: The compatibility shim sits in src/openai_compat and does not replace existing Redwood tool invocation paths. Key design decisions: 1) tool schema mapping: we prioritize field name compatibility, but will coerce types (string->number when unambiguous) and attach validation errors as assistant messages rather than 400s to mirror OpenAI's behavior; 2) tool_choice semantics: when the model suggests multiple candidate tools via a 'tool_choice' object, we convert that into a ranked list and emit a single 'invocation.started' for the chosen tool but include the alternatives as metadata on invocation.finished (avoids changing the runtime routing); 3) streaming fragmentation: many OpenAI clients expect each SSE event to correspond to a meaningful delta. We implemented a reassembler that maintains a minimal buffer keyed by request id, performs safe incremental JSON decoding for partial tool outputs (handles arrays/objects/strings that cross chunk boundaries), and emits assembled deltas when they parse or when a backpressure timeout fires (configurable, default 30ms).

Backward compatibility & migration: Existing Redwood clients are unaffected. OpenAI-compatible clients using the hosted endpoint will see slightly different assistant messages for tool lifecycles (invocation.started/finished wrappers). We added a feature flag to toggle the shim per-tenant for staged rollout. Docs and examples: docs/openai-compatibility.md contains mapping tables and sample SSE logs; examples/openai-proxy/README.md shows a canonical prompt + expected streamed output.

Testing & perf: Added unit tests for mapping edgecases (nullable arrays, polymorphic enums). Integration tests spin up the proxy with a small fake tool and assert the streamed assistant+tool messages match expectations. Perf bench shows median latency impact of ~+4% when the shim is enabled due to extra framing, but overall throughput is unchanged. We will monitor via REDWOOD-OPENAI-COMPAT metrics.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement schema mapping rules and explicit coercion policy
- [x] Implement streaming reassembly and safe incremental JSON decode
- [x] Add tests (unit + integration)
- [x] Docs + migration notes
- [x] Feature flag and rollout plan

Release notes (high level): This patch adds an OpenAI compatibility adapter for function/tool calling and improves streamed tool output stability for OpenAI-style clients. No breaking changes to Redwood-native APIs.

Related: Linear ENG-3589 (OpenAI compat alpha), ENG-3621 (streaming reassembly), incident SUP-1421 (customer reported truncated tool responses in streaming mode).
review_thread: Liam Ortega: Nice work — the mapping table in docs clarifies a lot. Two asks: please add a comment in the reassembler about the timeout heuristic and add a unit test for a string that contains multi-byte UTF-8 sequences split across chunks.
Maya Chen: Added test for multi-byte boundary case and expanded comment. Also increased default reassembly timeout to 30ms to reduce false flushes.
Priya Nair: Behavior question: when model returns tool_choice with two equal-score alternatives, do we pick one deterministically? We should ensure determinism for canary and replay.
Maya Chen: Deterministic tie-breaker implemented: lexicographic on tool id after score. Documented in mapping doc.
Arjun Singh: CI flagged a race in integration tests where two concurrent requests reuse the same buffer id. Please ensure buffer keyed by request+attempt.
Maya Chen: Fixed bug — buffer now keyed by (request_id, attempt_id). Re-ran tests; all green.
Priya Nair: Approved after the fix.
release_notes: Adds OpenAI-compatible function/tool calling adapter and robust streaming fragment reassembly. Feature gated per-tenant for staged rollout. No breaking changes to Redwood-native API.
